coach_briefing: SPM reconstruction supports the planned six-work/ five-recovery structure. Intervals 1–4 and 6 met their rate targets and each recovery was within 3–5 minutes. The material execution deviation is work-05 at 19.99 SPM, below its 22–24 SPM target; it was also slower than work-04. A tailwind-to-headwind shift overlaps the later intervals and may be associated with this speed change, but does not establish cause. Confirm resistance-band use separately; prescribed 1 km completion cannot be verified from these reconstructed distances.

deviations.description: Average stroke rate was 19.99 SPM versus the prescribed 22–24 SPM for this second-block work interval.

limitations: Time alignment alone cannot determine whether wind caused the speed change.
The environmental evidence cannot establish athlete improvement or regression.
environment_assessment.summary: Effective wind shifted from a 1.0 m/s tailwind at the start (effective headwind −1.0 m/s) to a 5.5 m/s headwind, crossing from tailwind to headwind at approximately 1800 s. This timing overlaps the later work intervals and supports an association with the observed speed changes, including the slower work-05; it does not establish causation or athlete regression.

follow_up_questions: Was the resistance band used for work intervals 1–3 and removed before interval 4?

prescribed_blocks: 3 × 1 km at 19–21 SPM with resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery.
3 × 1 km at 22–24 SPM without resistance band; 180–300 s active recovery.
plan_summary.summary: Plan: 6 × 1 km, with the first three work intervals at 19–21 SPM using a resistance band and the last three at 22–24 SPM without it; active recovery prescribed for 180–300 seconds between intervals.

session_associations.reason: The GPS recordings spatially match despite a preserved 37-second clock-start offset; route evidence supports a common outing rather than clock equality.
